_source: groundSpring Experiment 004 — Sequencing Depth and Taxonomic Noise
_references: Thompson et al. (2017) A communal catalogue reveals Earth's multiscale microbial diversity. Nature 551:457-463 (Earth Microbiome Project)
Lozupone & Knight (2005) UniFrac: a New Phylogenetic Method for Comparing Microbial Communities. Appl.Environ.Microbiol. 71(12):8228-8235

_provenance.generated_by: Synthetic community based on published soil microbiome profiles
_provenance.data_origin: Synthetic 150-genus log-normal community modeled after EMP agricultural soil profiles. No real 16S sequences used. Phase 0+ target: SRA accession from EMP (e.g. PRJEB11419) or Zenodo mock community (e.g. doi:10.5281/zenodo.3731344).
_provenance.real_data_accession: Pending: EMP SRA PRJEB11419 or ZymoBIOMICS Mock Community (SRR7732181)
_provenance.notes: Community structure modeled after typical agricultural soil 16S profiles. Log-normal genus abundances within phyla. Expected ranges from multinomial sampling theory with seed=42.

_description: Simulated rarefaction analysis to characterize the noise floor of 16S rRNA taxonomic assignment
_groundspring_question: At what sequencing depth does taxonomy become stable? When does more sequencing stop helping?

reference_community._description: Synthetic but ecologically realistic soil microbiome community from Michigan agricultural soil
reference_community._note: Based on typical 16S profiles reported in agricultural soil studies. Genus-level abundances are log-normally distributed.

phylum_stability.description: At what depth are all 8 phyla consistently detected?

genus_saturation.description: At what depth does genus count stop increasing meaningfully?
genus_saturation.saturation_criterion: < 5% new genera per doubling of depth

shannon_convergence.description: At what depth does Shannon diversity stabilize within 5% of true value?
